- **Separating remaining work:** ran non-heavy packages and vet once, retaining native build coverage.

- **Preserving caches and semantics:** retained module/build caches while clearing test-result caches; kept Go’s default parallelism.

content.text:
Not in the versions checked—the difference is **how the array is passed**.

| Expression | Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Azure VM) | PowerShell 7.5.4 (local) |
|---|---|---|
| `ConvertTo-Json -InputObject @(0)` | `[0]` | `[0]` |
| `@(0) \| ConvertTo-Json` | `0` | `0` |

PowerShell’s issue tracker documents the same behavior in [7.2.6](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/18203).

Our workflow explicitly constructs an array and passes `-InputObject`, so the finding appears to confuse it with pipeline behavior. Adding its suggested `-AsArray` produces **`[[0]]`** on 7.5.4, introducing unwanted nesting.

I haven’t directly tested 7.6.5, which the [current Windows runner image lists](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-Readme.md), but found no evidence of a relevant version change.
